_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — sender-identity-secrets-writeonly (integriq#1983 review 5260087915, blocker 2). SECURITY FIX. `sender_identity.smimePrivateKey` holds the PEM private key this identity signs mail with. Its own description claimed 'Write only; it is never read back over the API' and NOTHING enforced that: no `writeOnly`, no schema `authorization` block, no fragment. Combined with OpenRegister's read default — `DEFAULT_CLOSED_WRITE_ACTIONS` is create/update/delete/destroy as of OpenRegister 2.1.22 (`destroy` was added 2026-09-14 in openregister#3724; it is create/update/delete on 2.0.x), and `read` is in neither list, so `read` is granted when no authorization block is present — the signing key was returned to any authenticated account on the instance. Whoever reads it can sign mail as the organisation. `writeOnly: true` makes OpenRegister's render boundary strip the field from EVERY API response (admin included, body and `@self.relations` index copy alike, list and search included). A field the server never returns cannot leak, whoever reads it. THE CONSUMER WAS SWITCHED IN THE SAME CHANGE, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT TAKES TWO FLAGS: writeOnly stripping happens in OpenRegister's RENDER pass, not in the RBAC check — `RenderObject::doWriteOnly` is computed from the schema alone and has no `_rbac` term — so `_rbac: false` alone does NOT defeat it and `find()` renders by default. SenderIdentityService therefore reads with `_rbac: false` AND `_render: false`. Getting this wrong (integriq#2104 review 5264751700, blocker 1) means OutboundSecurityService::protect() observes an empty key, reports 'This identity is set to sign but carries no S/MIME certificate and key', and sends the message UNSIGNED under a reason that reads like an unconfigured identity. `smimeCertificate` is deliberately NOT marked: a certificate is public material and an operator must be able to inspect what an identity signs with. `smimePrivateKeyRef` is deliberately NOT marked either — a reference is not a secret, and a write-only reference would make a signing failure undiagnosable.
